mc97249d201: Your kid gets a phone call from the North Pole. You get the full backstage tour — what's actually happening, how it's kept safe, and how to make the moment land perfectly.
mb7a0efe088: When your child calls, they're talking to a live AI performance of Santa — a video avatar with a warm, unhurried voice, holding a real two-way conversation in real time. Nothing is pre-recorded and no two calls are the same. Before the call, you tell us your child's name and, if you like, their age, city, wish list, and something good they did this year. Santa opens with their name and works those details in naturally — that's the moment jaws drop.
mf3441e5ee5: You control recordings. Calls are not recorded automatically. On supported calls, you can record locally and choose whether to save the video to Photos. Provider processing of call audio and transcripts is separate; account deletion requests provider cleanup with the limits described in our full privacy policy.
m38287c6686: Santa never asks for personal information. He's instructed not to ask where your child lives, what school they attend, or anything of the sort — you provide the personal touches, never the child.
m03802fe1ef: No gift promises. Santa is warm and encouraging about wish lists but never commits to delivering a specific present. That promise stays yours to make.
mfd6e2c312d: A parental gate stands in front of anything involving money or leaving the app — kids can't buy minutes or wander to the web.
ma847745d06: Calls have a natural end. Santa and Mrs. Claus calls can last up to six minutes; Comet calls up to three. Your available minutes also limit the length of each call.
m85164cc036: Fill in the wish list beforehand. One or two real items your child actually asked for. Hearing Santa already knows is the whole trick.
m014da0243f: Add a good deed. For example: "I heard you helped your little brother learn to ride his bike…" A real detail makes the conversation personal.
m1df9d91afd: Stay in the room. Partly for safety, mostly because you'll want to see their face. Prop the phone up rather than holding it — it feels more like a real video call.
ma246a10da5: Let the call end naturally. Santa wraps up on his own as time runs low. Resist the urge to stretch it — a great four-minute call beats a padded six.
m976301bd47: Ages 3 and up. Three-to-eight is the sweet spot for full belief; older kids often enjoy it as a delightful bit of theater with younger siblings.
m71018442b9: Our suggestion: "It's the way Santa makes video calls this time of year — he can't fly everywhere before Christmas Eve." Keep the answer in the world of the story. Dial Santa never breaks character on a call.
m8443476560: You buy a minute pack once — no subscription — and minutes never expire. Calls are metered by the second, and if Santa ever fails to answer or a call won't connect, those minutes come straight back. Anything ever feels off, support is a human who'll fix it fast.

mb838650df8: Dial Santa ("we," "us") is a parent-directed entertainment app: a grown-up sets everything up and buys minutes, and a child uses it together with their parent or guardian. This policy covers the Dial Santa iOS app and this website.
m40313a7469: Parent email address. This is your account. We use it to sign you in (a one-time code, no password), attach your purchased minutes, and send purchase receipts. Joining the website launch waitlist is a separate, optional choice.
mc09bcb9f2d: Call personalization you provide. A child's first name, and optionally an age, city, wish list, or good deeds — whatever a parent chooses to enter. These exist so Santa can greet your child and hold a real conversation.
made1a5b86e: Purchase records. Which minute pack you bought and when. Payments are handled by Apple for in-app purchases and Stripe for website purchases — we never see or store card numbers.
m387272c049: Basic call records. When a call happened and how long it lasted, so we can meter minutes correctly and refund calls that fail.
ma073858370: The website waitlist is for adults. If you join, we save your email address, signup date, and the consent you gave so we can send you one email when Dial Santa launches. ma18ceae4e1: Waitlist addresses are stored in our Railway database until we send the launch announcement or you ask us to remove yours. To leave the waitlist before launch, email hohoho@dialsanta.app. Deleting an app account also removes the matching waitlist address. We briefly store a keyed, unreadable version of the signup IP address to limit spam; it expires after one hour.
mccb7ce6ddb: You can choose your website language using the language selector. Your selection is saved locally in your browser and included in links so you can keep the same language as you browse. We do not request your location.
m28cf44d09b: Calls are live conversations with an AI character. The parent email screen displays a linked footer: “By continuing, you confirm you have read and agree to our privacy policy, terms & conditions, and EULA.” Choosing Continue stages that acceptance; it is recorded after the same email address is verified. Existing signed-in users without a current acceptance receive Continue and Not now with the same linked footer before a call; email reverification is not required solely for that acceptance. AI data sharing and provider names are explained in this policy, without a separate AI-sharing panel in the app. iOS microphone permission is separate. Your child’s voice is processed in real time so the character can hear and respond. The camera self-view stays on your device; it is not sent to the AI providers or our servers. An optional local recording includes that self-view.
me25492e528: Recording is off by default. Optional screen-and-voice recordings stay on your device. ElevenLabs voice recording is disabled; its agents are configured to delete conversation audio and transcript data with zero-day retention. This is not ElevenLabs' enterprise Zero Retention Mode. LiveAvatar can retain transcripts, session records and personalized contexts. Account deletion requests removal of ElevenLabs conversations and LiveAvatar contexts/events and verifies the LiveAvatar transcript is empty. It stops LemonSlice sessions; it does not verify deletion of any historical LemonSlice logs or media. Provider technical, security, billing and legally required records may have separate retention.
mf5c6cd5256: Starting a call sends Dial Santa the child's first name, optional age, city, wish list and good deeds, and selected language. Our backend passes the relevant details to the providers below to personalize the conversation. Spoken words, transcripts and generated replies may also contain personal information. Please share only what you want the character to know.
mf1caa3ce51: Santa is designed never to ask a child for personal information, and never to promise specific gifts.
m499003f5b2: On supported calls, Record captures the call screen, including the camera self-view, and both sides of the conversation. A visible recording control lets you stop recording. Muting your microphone also mutes your voice in the recording. Recording stops when the call ends or the app goes into the background.
mf74b8c95d3: Recordings are temporary files on your device. Dial Santa does not upload them to our servers or use them for advertising. After the call, you can preview, delete, or choose Save to Photos. Saving requests permission only to add a video to your library, not to read your existing photos. If saving fails or permission is denied, the recording remains available on the call's end screen so you can try again.
mc817571199: Save a recording to Photos if you want to keep it. Unsaved recordings are removed when you discard them, leave the call's review screen after confirming deletion, or restart the app. Videos saved to Photos are controlled by your Photos and iCloud settings. Deleting your Dial Santa account does not delete videos you saved to Photos; delete those in Photos yourself.
m3d5a402f84: These companies support the app. The call providers receive the following data for the stated purposes:
m3a2ce6bb45: ElevenLabs processes microphone audio, transcripts and personalization to generate replies and voices for Santa, Mrs. Claus and Comet. Its language-model processing uses OpenAI with conversation and profile text, including when an alternative model is needed. HeyGen (LiveAvatar) receives generated speech to animate Santa and Mrs. Claus; a fallback call mode also processes microphone audio, transcripts and personalization there. LemonSlice (Infinity AI, Inc.) receives generated speech to animate Comet. Generated speech can repeat details shared during the call.
m3c041fb233: LiveKit transports Santa and Mrs. Claus calls; Daily transports Comet calls. They carry encrypted microphone audio, character audio/video, captions, transcript events and session identifiers. This does not include your camera self-view. Providers also process connection and service-operation information.
mfed83b1eb9: Apple, Stripe and RevenueCat — Apple and Stripe process purchases and receipts through their respective payment services. RevenueCat receives an opaque account identifier and Apple transaction information to verify and report in-app purchases. We do not send RevenueCat child profiles, voice recordings or call content. When you delete your account, we request deletion of its RevenueCat customer record.
m102f1748d9: Railway — hosts our servers and database (located in the United States).
m7eafcfedba: Meta — measures which Dial Santa ads led to app installs. Once, after a parent signs up and verifies their email, Meta's SDK in the app sends an install and app-open event with basic device information (such as device model, iOS version, language, time zone, and an app-specific anonymous ID). The SDK doesn't start again when the app is opened later. Meta receives this device's advertising identifier only if you allow tracking when iOS asks. Automatic event logging, automatic advanced matching, and Meta crash reports are turned off, and Meta's Limited Data Use setting is on. We do not send child profiles, names, ages, voice, call content, email addresses, account details, or purchases to Meta. Information Meta has already received is handled under Meta's own policies.
m7aacc42d86: Provider protections include encrypted transmission and the security, access and rights commitments in their applicable terms. The data-processing terms of HeyGen, ElevenLabs, LiveKit and Daily address processing instructions, confidentiality, security and subprocessors. Their scope and retention rules differ. We never sell personal information.
mf53da45aed: Dial Santa is built for parents to run. Accounts, purchases, and setup are done by an adult; a parental gate protects anything involving money, privacy controls, or leaving the app. We collect from children only what a parent enters on their behalf (like a first name), plus the real-time voice processing described above — after the parent accepts the linked account terms and privacy policy as described above. Dial Santa does not show third-party ads. Advertising measurement is accepted by the parent at sign-up, happens once after the parent's email is verified, can be turned off under Parents, and never receives child profile or call data. We follow the principles of COPPA: minimal collection, parental consent, no behavioral advertising to children, and parental control over deletion.
mbaf9fd3aa7: Delete your account: open Parents → Account → Delete account, verify your email and confirm. We remove your account email, minute balance and call records from our active database and clear the child profile and history on that device. Other signed-in devices are signed out and clear their local account data when they next contact our server. Call-provider cleanup runs automatically in the background and retries temporary failures. Cleanup usually takes a few minutes; temporary outages can take longer. Check Parents → Account for a completion confirmation, or contact support.
m52dd1d64b5: Sign out: open Parents → Account → Sign out. Purchased minutes remain with your email, while the child profile and local history are removed from that device.
mbf9e643098: See your data: contact support to request access.
m4ba066eb97: Stop future call sharing: end any active call and do not start another AI call. You can sign out under Parents → Account; this prevents new online calls on that device until you sign in again. Offline Activities remain available. Build 40 has no Parents AI-sharing toggle. Stopping calls or signing out does not erase data already processed. Use account deletion or contact support for deletion requests.
maf85d078dd: Advertising measurement: open Parents → Privacy & safety → Turn off ad measurement. Dial Santa then shares nothing more with Meta from that device, even if you sign in again, and you stay signed in. You can also decline Apple's tracking prompt, or turn off Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking, to withhold the advertising identifier. Some U.S. state privacy laws may treat sharing device information for ad measurement as "sharing" personal information; the Parents control is how you opt out on your device, and you can also email us.
m8d29181fca: Account deletion removes unused minutes and does not automatically issue a refund. Contact support for help with a refund.
m4a74443bc7: All traffic is encrypted in transit (HTTPS/TLS). Sign-in codes are stored only as one-way hashes and expire in 10 minutes. We keep account and purchase records while your account exists and as required for tax and accounting; call-metering records are kept only as long as needed for billing accuracy. After account deletion, we retain keyed account digests and payment references to prevent old credentials or duplicate payment notifications from restoring an erased account. Payment processors may retain transaction records. Temporary provider-erasure jobs retain the references needed to complete downstream deletion; they are removed after completion. Provider cleanup follows the limits explained above; separate technical, security or legal records may remain under provider terms.

seo.guides.intro: Practical guides for your family’s next Santa conversation.
seo.facetime.question: Can we use FaceTime to call Santa?
seo.facetime.answer: Dial Santa is a separate iPhone app for live AI video conversations. It does not use Apple FaceTime and does not provide a Santa phone number. A grown-up sets up the app and buys call minutes.
seo.analytics.title: Website analytics
seo.analytics.body: Optional page and App Store click counts help us improve this website. Off until you allow them. No recordings or app-account details. Your browser’s privacy signals take priority.
seo.privacy.title: Optional website analytics
seo.privacy.body: Website analytics is off by default. If you allow it using the website footer, we send PostHog (US hosting) a page category, language, broad referring-source category and App Store button position. A random identifier lasts only for the current page; it is not linked to your app account. We do not send names, email addresses, child profiles, call content, form entries, full referral URLs or URL query parameters. This analytics feature uses no advertising cookies, session replay or automatic interaction capture; the Meta Pixel described below is separate and has its own control. PostHog necessarily receives network information when a request reaches its service; our event configuration disables location enrichment and IP-address storage in event properties. Your analytics choice is saved locally. You can stop future counts in the footer; this does not erase previously received events. We honor Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track. App Store links contain a shared website campaign label, not a personal identifier, so Apple can provide campaign reports under its own privacy policy. Contact us with questions or data requests.
ads.choice.title: Advertising measurement
ads.choice.body: The Meta Pixel tells us whether our Facebook and Instagram ads bring parents here and lets us show Dial Santa ads to people who visited. It receives standard browsing information, a Meta cookie and which App Store button was tapped — never child profiles, app accounts, form entries or call content. In the EU, UK and Switzerland it stays off until you allow it. Your browser’s privacy signals turn it off.
ads.banner.body: We use the Meta Pixel to measure our ads and show Dial Santa to parents who might enjoy it. It receives browsing information and a Meta cookie — never child profiles, app accounts or call content.
privacy.ads.title: Advertising measurement on this website
privacy.ads.body: This website uses the Meta Pixel so we can measure whether our Facebook and Instagram ads bring parents to dialsanta.app and show Dial Santa ads to people who have visited. While it runs, Meta receives the pages you view, which App Store button you tap, browser and device information, your IP address and a Meta cookie that lasts up to 90 days; Meta may link this with your Meta account under Meta’s own privacy policy. We do not send names, email addresses, child profiles, app accounts, form entries or call content. Meta’s automatic advanced matching, automatic event collection and automatic configuration are turned off, and Meta’s Limited Data Use setting is on where it applies. If your browser’s time zone is in the EU, UK or Switzerland, the Pixel stays off until you choose Allow in the banner; elsewhere it runs unless you turn it off. You can change your choice anytime under Advertising measurement in the website footer, and we honor Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track. Turning it off stops future sharing but does not erase information Meta already received. The Pixel does not run on checkout or confirmation pages or inside the app.
privacy.ads.update: October 7, 2026: added the Meta Pixel on this website, with a consent banner in Europe and an Advertising measurement control in the footer.
privacy.appanalytics.title: Optional app analytics
privacy.appanalytics.body: In app versions offering “Help improve Dial Santa”, this separate choice is off by default. If a parent enables it, our API sends PostHog (US hosting) selected app steps, verification and onboarding outcomes, language, selected character, referral category, call connection outcomes, optional feedback choices, and verified purchase or refund amounts, products and currencies. Random app and parent-account identifiers connect these events across sessions and signed-in devices. These identifiers are pseudonymous, not anonymous: our service can associate the parent ID with the account. Website measurement is not linked to it. We do not send names, email addresses, child profiles, form entries, call audio, transcripts, video, recordings or advertising identifiers to PostHog. There is no session replay or automatic interaction capture. Location enrichment is disabled; events reach PostHog through our server.
privacy.appanalytics.controls: Turn off Help improve Dial Santa in Parents to stop future app events from that device. The account preference reaches our server when the device reconnects; already received events are not erased by turning it off. Signing out clears the local analytics queue and rotates the device’s random ID. Account deletion queues removal of the linked PostHog person and events and reports cleanup as pending until verified. Events never linked to an account may remain; contact support for data requests. Analytics records are kept for product reporting until deletion or the applicable retention period. This choice does not affect calling, purchases or access to Activities.
privacy.appanalytics.update: October 7, 2026: described optional PostHog app analytics for app versions that offer the Help improve Dial Santa control.
guide.facetime-santa.title: Can You FaceTime Santa? A Parent’s Guide | Dial Santa
guide.facetime-santa.description: Looking to FaceTime Santa? Learn how live Santa video calls work, how they differ from Apple FaceTime, and what to check before your child calls.
guide.facetime-santa.heading: Can you FaceTime Santa?
guide.facetime-santa.intro: You want the part that matters: your child asks a question, Santa hears it, and he answers. Here’s how to find that kind of Santa video call—and what to know before you start.
guide.facetime-santa.body.0: A Santa video call, on your iPhone
guide.facetime-santa.body.1: People often say “FaceTime Santa” when they mean a face-to-face video conversation with Santa. Dial Santa offers a live, two-way conversation with an AI Santa in its own iPhone app. It does not use Apple’s FaceTime service, and you do not need Santa’s phone number or email address.
guide.facetime-santa.body.2: There is no public Santa FaceTime number provided by Dial Santa. To use the app, a parent downloads it from the App Store, sets up the account and profile, chooses call minutes, and starts a call inside Dial Santa.
guide.facetime-santa.body.3: What kind of Santa call are you looking for?
guide.facetime-santa.body.4:
Three different ways to bring Santa into your home
ExperienceWhat happensWhat to check
Prerecorded messageA prepared video or phone message plays.Which details are personalized, and whether your child can actually ask questions.
Live performerA human performer talks to your family during a booked appointment.Availability, booking terms, duration, price and the video service used.
Live AI conversationAn AI character responds to what your child says in the moment.Adult supervision, voice-data handling, device support and call-minute pricing.
guide.facetime-santa.body.5: Dial Santa is the third option. Its Santa is an AI character, not a human performer. It is designed for a parent or guardian to set up and enjoy with their child.
guide.facetime-santa.body.7:
1. Download on iPhone. The app requires iOS 17 or later and an internet connection.
  2. Set up as the grown-up. Verify your email and read the app’s linked policies. Add a first name and, if you choose, a wish or a good deed.
  3. Choose minutes. The download is free; calls use purchased minutes. The five-minute pack is US$2.99 in the US App Store. Local prices may vary.
  4. Get comfortable together. Start the call inside the app and let your child ask a question. Santa responds to their voice; the camera is a self-view that stays on the device.
guide.facetime-santa.body.8: For a fuller setup checklist, see how to call Santa.
guide.facetime-santa.body.10: Different Santa services have different prices. Dial Santa is free to download, but its live calls require paid minutes through Apple in-app purchases. Packs are 5 minutes for US$2.99, 12 for US$5.99 or 30 for US$15.99. There is no subscription, and unused minutes never expire. Check the price shown in your App Store before buying.
guide.facetime-santa.body.12: In Dial Santa, Santa responds to speech and the details a parent provides. The camera is a local self-view; it is not sent to the AI providers or our servers. Call audio and personalization are processed by service providers as described in the privacy policy. Avoid sharing addresses, school names or other details you do not want processed.
guide.facetime-santa.body.14: Have one question ready: “What do the reindeer eat?” is easier to start with than a long list. Keep the room quiet, stay beside your child, and let them take their time. A child who only wants to listen can enjoy a short hello; there is no need to push them to perform.
guide.facetime-santa.body.15: Try our questions to ask Santa or read the parents’ guide before the call.
guide.facetime-santa.body.16: FaceTime is a trademark of Apple Inc. Dial Santa is an independent app and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple.
guide.how-to-call-santa.title: How to Call Santa on iPhone: Setup, Cost & Tips | Dial Santa
guide.how-to-call-santa.description: A practical guide to calling Santa with Dial Santa: parent setup, iPhone requirements, minute packs, privacy and simple tips for your first live AI call.
guide.how-to-call-santa.heading: How to call Santa on your iPhone
guide.how-to-call-santa.intro: A quiet corner, one good question, and a grown-up nearby. Here’s how to get ready for your family’s first live AI Santa conversation with Dial Santa.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.1: A Santa hotline, a prerecorded message, an appointment with a human performer and a live AI video call are different experiences. Dial Santa is a live AI conversation: your child speaks and the character responds in the moment. It happens inside the iPhone app, not by dialing a telephone number or using Apple FaceTime.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.3:
• An iPhone running iOS 17 or later and a reliable internet connection.
  • A parent or guardian to create the account, choose purchases and stay with the child.
  • Access to the parent’s email for sign-in verification.
  • Purchased call minutes and permission to use the microphone.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.5: Use the official Dial Santa App Store listing. Downloading the app is free. Calls require minutes bought inside the app through Apple; downloading alone does not start a subscription.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.7: Follow the email verification steps in the app and read the linked privacy policy and terms. A parent handles setup. The app’s parental gate protects purchases and settings, but it does not replace adult supervision during a conversation.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.9: Enter a first name. You can also add a wish or a good deed, such as helping a sibling or learning something new. You do not need to write a script. Share only details you are comfortable having processed for the call; avoid a home address, school name or sensitive family information.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.11: US minute packs are 5 minutes for US$2.99, 12 for US$5.99 and 30 for US$15.99. Local App Store prices may vary. Minutes never expire, and there is no subscription. Santa is included; Mrs. Claus and Comet each require a separate US$0.99 character unlock in the US, plus purchased call minutes.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.12: Santa and Mrs. Claus calls can last up to six minutes each; Comet calls can last up to three. Your available balance can make the call shorter. Minutes are metered by the connected second, so unused time stays in your account.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.14: Find a quiet spot, turn up the volume, and allow the microphone when the app asks. Choose the character and start the call. Santa hears and responds to speech. The camera view lets your family see themselves on the device; it is not sent to our servers or the AI providers.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.15: Begin with a simple hello. If your child goes quiet, you can help with “We were wondering how the reindeer get ready for Christmas.” Follow the child’s pace and end the call whenever you need to.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.17: Try a short conversation first so you can judge the experience for your family. Call languages vary by character and installed app version. Check the language picker in the app before buying minutes.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.19:
• Check the internet connection and the app’s microphone permission in iPhone Settings.
  • Confirm there are minutes available and that the selected character is unlocked.
  • If you cannot hear the character, check volume and the audio device your iPhone is using.
  • If the problem continues, use Dial Santa support. Describe the issue and approximate time without sending child recordings or sign-in codes.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.21: Recording is optional and off by default. On supported calls, you can record locally and choose whether to save the video to Photos. Provider processing of call audio and transcripts is separate from that local recording feature. Read the privacy policy for recipients, retention and deletion limits.
guide.how-to-call-santa.body.22: For conversation ideas, explore questions to ask Santa. Wondering about FaceTime? Our Santa video-call comparison explains the difference.
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.title: 24 Questions to Ask Santa on a Video Call | Dial Santa
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.description: Help your child start a Santa conversation with 24 playful questions about reindeer, the North Pole and Christmas, plus tips for shy first-time callers.
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.heading: 24 questions to ask Santa
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.intro: The best question is the one your child is curious about. Keep a few of these nearby for the moment they look at Santa and forget everything they wanted to say.
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.body.1:
1. What have you been doing today?
  2. What is your favorite kind of cookie?
  3. Is it snowing at the North Pole?
  4. What makes you laugh?
  5. Do you have a favorite Christmas song?
  6. What do you do when you need a rest?
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.body.3:
1. What do the reindeer eat for breakfast?
  2. How do the reindeer practice flying?
  3. Which reindeer likes to play games?
  4. Do the reindeer get snow on their noses?
  5. How do you keep the reindeer warm?
  6. What happens when a reindeer sneezes?
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.body.4: For a peek around the North Pole
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.body.5:
1. What does the workshop sound like?
  2. What do the elves do on their days off?
  3. Who helps you check the sleigh?
  4. Does Mrs. Claus have a favorite recipe?
  5. What is the funniest thing that happened in the workshop?
  6. If I visited the North Pole, what would you show me first?
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.body.7:
1. What is a kind thing I could do for someone this week?
  2. Can I tell you something I learned?
  3. Would you like to hear about my favorite Christmas tradition?
  4. How do you choose a present for someone you love?
  5. What would you put in a snowman’s lunchbox?
  6. What should we say to the reindeer before you go?
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.body.9: Let them listen first. You can ask the opening question together or let a toy “ask” it. Give them room to decide whether to speak. A short, relaxed hello is enough; there is no need to use every question or make the moment perfect.
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.body.11: Pick one or two favorites. If Santa talks about cookies, “Who helps bake them?” is a natural next question. Leave a little space after each answer. A conversation about one wonderfully important reindeer detail can be more fun than racing through twenty-four questions.
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.body.13: A wish list can be part of the story without becoming a promise. Help children talk about what they enjoy, who they care about and what they have learned. In Dial Santa, the AI character is instructed not to promise specific gifts. A grown-up should stay nearby because AI replies can be imperfect.
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.body.15: Dial Santa is an iPhone app for live, two-way conversations with an AI Santa. A parent sets up the profile and buys call minutes. The download is free; US minute packs start at US$2.99 for five minutes, with no subscription. Santa responds to voice, while the camera is a local self-view.
guide.questions-to-ask-santa.body.16: Read how to call Santa for setup, device requirements and pricing, or visit the parents’ guide. For how call audio is processed, see our privacy policy.
